cues: Haloalkanes are primary, secondary or tertiary by the carbon holding the halogen.
They are best made from alcohols, with thionyl chloride.
Boiling points rise from fluoride to iodide and fall with branching.
S N two is one step, second order, with inversion, favoured by methyl and primary halides.
S N one goes through a carbocation, is first order, gives racemisation, and is favoured by tertiary halides.
Potassium salts attack through carbon or oxygen, silver salts through nitrogen.
Aqueous potash substitutes, alcoholic potash eliminates.
And chloroform, made from propanone and bleaching powder, must be protected from light and air.
text: Let us recap. Haloalkanes are primary, secondary or tertiary by the carbon holding the halogen. They are best made from alcohols, with thionyl chloride. Boiling points rise from fluoride to iodide and fall with branching. S N two is one step, second order, with inversion, favoured by methyl and primary halides. S N one goes through a carbocation, is first order, gives racemisation, and is favoured by tertiary halides. Potassium salts attack through carbon or oxygen, silver salts through nitrogen. Aqueous potash substitutes, alcoholic potash eliminates. And chloroform, made from propanone and bleaching powder, must be protected from light and air.
